note: Fresh English held-out set for the sample-interview bank, written 2026-11-12 before any score of it was computed and before the new accept rule was chosen. Never used for tuning: rule_search.py tunes on blind_set.json + en_near.json and reports these separately. `paraphrases`: two new phrasings per entry. `near`: questions on (or shaped like) an entry's topic that ask something the entry does not answer; `near` names the entry they resemble. `offbank`: interview questions the bank does not cover.

b001: Could you start by introducing yourself and what you've done so far?
Give me a short overview of your professional journey.
b002: What makes Halden Freight Systems interesting to you?
Why did you decide to apply for this job with us?
b003: Can you describe the Lantern system you worked on?
What exactly was the invoice extraction project you ran?
b004: What did Lantern achieve in the end?
What measurable outcomes came out of the Lantern work?
b005: What would you say is an area where you still need to grow?
Which of your habits at work would a manager want you to change?
b006: Which engineering decision are you proudest of, and what did it cost you?
Can you give an example of a trade-off you consciously accepted in a design?
b007: Could you explain the routing tool you made for the courier pilot?
What did the route optimisation pilot involve on your side?
b008: How much do you know about Halden and what we sell?
Have you had a look at our product before this interview?
b009: How do you make sure an LLM feature is good enough to ship?
What testing do you do on a language model system before it goes live?
b010: What do you do when the model gives a wrong or uncertain answer?
How do you catch bad outputs from the LLM before they cause damage?
b011: What accuracy did the Lantern pipeline achieve?
How often did Lantern extract the fields correctly?
b012: What did running the pipeline cost, and did it pay off?
Was the money spent on the model calls worth it in the end?
b013: How would you design a dispatcher that uses an LLM?
If you joined, how would you add language models to our dispatch tooling?
b014: Is there anything you'd like to ask us?
Before we wrap up, what questions do you have for me?
b015: How soon would you be available to start?
If we offered you the job, when could you begin?
b016: What salary range are you expecting?
What kind of pay are you hoping for in this role?
b017: How much experience do you have putting LLMs into production?
Have you run language model systems for real users?
b018: How does your background connect to our route planning work?
What in your experience is relevant to routing and logistics?
b019: How did you decide when to use a small model versus a big one?
What was your approach to picking between cheaper and stronger models?
b020: How do you usually kick off a new project from scratch?
What are your first steps when you build a prototype?
b021: Have you built any automation into your release process?
Did you automate parts of how you deploy software?
b022: What do you understand by ETA drift?
Could you tell me what ETA drift means?
